titulo: Maha Mantra Kirtan Before Brunch: Tell Your Karma I Said Hi
caption:
Maha Mantra Kirtan Before Brunch: Tell Your Karma I Said Hi

Cella here, front and center, because someone has to be. No hands, so the drum is strapped to my chest. Very devout. Very photogenic.

Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare, Hare Rāma Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma Hare Hare.

What it is: the Hare Krishna maha mantra ("great mantra"), sixteen names from the Kali-Santarana Upanishad, sung every day in the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition and carried around the world by ISKCON since 1966. (Sung in the order ISKCON chants it; the Upanishad lists Hare Rāma first.) Say it HAH-ray, KRISH-nuh, RAH-muh. This is kirtan, the way it is sung in a group: a lead voice, a group answering, a drum and a harmonium.

In the tradition: Hare addresses Harā, the Lord's energy; Kṛṣṇa and Rāma are names of God. Prabhupada read the whole mantra as a prayer: "O Supreme Energy of the Lord, O Lord Krishna, please kindly engage me in your transcendental service." The English words on screen follow that reading.

Why a sound like this may calm you: in a 2001 BMJ study, 23 healthy adults recited a yoga mantra (om-mani-padme-om) and the rosary; both slowed breathing to about 6 breaths a minute, down from about 14, and strengthened the heart-rhythm reflex (Bernardi et al.). Limit: 23 healthy people, one session, and the authors are cautious about why it happens. Two more lean the same way, with limits (Perry 2024: 34 adults, no non-chanting group; Kalyani 2011: a pilot of 12 people); none tested this exact mantra. Small studies, short effects: calmer, not cured.

And if karma is real, this should clean a little of yours. If it isn't, you still spent 22 seconds on something kinder than your feed.

Sing it with the lead voice, one word to a beat. Then again.

Sources: Bernardi et al. 2001; Perry; Kalyani et al. 2011; Kali-Santarana Upanishad; Prabhupada; Chaitanya's Shikshashtaka; ISKCON Educational Services. Full references: YouTube description.

Voice and music: synthetic (ElevenLabs), AI voices and a band from takes NAOS already made; scene drawn by NAOS. Corrections from practitioners are welcome.
Closer to yourself.

alt: A 22.24-second vertical video of two small flat doorway-shaped characters, Cella and a friend, each with two white eyes and no hands, in an ashram courtyard at sunset with a thatched hut and a fig tree, wearing a pink sari with a white shawl, a white dhoti and a cream shawl and swaying side to side to a sung Hare Krishna maha mantra with a band and synthetic voices. Below them the mantra's words light up one by one in a gold capsule, and under each active word its English meaning appears (O energy of the Lord, The all-attractive One, The source of pleasure). The bottom of the screen is left clear for the app.
